newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU experts to discuss cereals area aid measures.
newsitem.headline: EU experts to discuss cereals area aid measures.

text.p: European Union experts are to discuss a series of cereals, oilseeds and protein crop area aid measures on Thursday, EU member state officials said.
The experts, meeting before the EU cereals management committee's weekly session, are due to discuss the impact of changes made to set-aside rules for the 1996 harvest.

The changes involved fixing a single rate for rotational and permanent set-aside at 10 percent of the total arable area. Previously farmers had to set aside 12 percent and 15 percent respectively of their land in rotational and permanent schemes.
Italy is expected to criticise a voluntary set-aside scheme which it argues favours northern farmers.

A proposal to change the Spanish and Portuguese base areas eligible for EU subsidies is also due to be discussed and a vote may be taken later on Thursday by the management committee. It involves decreasing the non-irrigated and increasing the irrigated area eligible for EU payments.
The experts are also due to discuss a Greek request that its irrigated area limit should be raised and a French demand to change the planting deadline for buckwheat.
A proposal to add an extra 40 to 50 oilseed varieties to an approved list will also be discussed and is expected to be voted on by the cereals management committee later on Thursday.
